title: Self-Dual Lattice Function
body_html:
Self-Dual Lattice Function

Let \(V\) carry a nondegenerate sesquilinear form. In the Loke-Ma normalization, the shifted dual of an \(o_D\)-lattice \(L\subseteq V\) is \[ L^\vee=\{v\in V:\langle v,L\rangle_V\subseteq\mathbf p_D\}. \] For a lattice function \(L\), the dual lattice function is \[ (L^\vee)_s=(L_{(-s)+})^\vee. \] The lattice function is self-dual when \(L=L^\vee\). Under the Bruhat-Tits identification for classical groups, building points correspond to splittable self-dual lattice functions.

The notation \(L^\vee\) here is deliberately separated from the hermitian \(o_D\)-dual \(L^\#\) and from the symplectic annihilator \(L^{\perp_\psi}\); see Dual Lattice Conventions.
